before.title: Distributor Oil Leak and Failure Causing No-Spark Condition
before.description: The KL-DE 2.5L V6 distributor is driven off the rear cylinder head and has internal and external O-ring seals that commonly fail with age. As the shaft bushings wear, oil migrates past the seals and pools inside the distributor cap, causing misfires, rough running, and ultimately no-spark crank-no-start conditions. RepairPal lists 'Crank but No Start Condition and No Spark' as the most commonly reported MX-6 problem, frequently traced to a failed distributor. Once the shaft itself develops play (wobble), the internal seal cannot be effectively replaced and the entire distributor must be replaced or rebuilt.
before.solution: Inspect the distributor cap for oil contamination. If only the external O-ring is leaking and shaft has no play, replace the small base O-ring (~$3) and the cap/rotor. If the shaft is worn or oil has reached the internal pickup, replace the distributor assembly (reman units approximately $200-$300 plus core). Always replace cap, rotor, and plug wires at the same time.
symptoms: Crank but no start, no spark
Oil pooled inside distributor cap
Oil drip below distributor onto transaxle
Misfires, rough running, hesitation under load
Intermittent stalling once warm

before.title: EGR Valve Carbon Buildup Causing Rough Idle and P0400 Codes
before.description: The KL-DE V6 EGR system is highly prone to carbon clogging. Soot accumulates inside the EGR valve diaphragm and inside the EGR passages cast into the throttle body and intake. When the valve sticks open, exhaust gas enters at idle and produces a rough, surging, or stalling idle with a CEL. Owners report that on the MX-6, P0400 (EGR flow insufficient) is the most common emissions code, and approximately 95% of the time it is a clogged valve or completely blocked EGR ports in the throttle body, not a failed component. Access is poor: the upper intake plenum and throttle body must usually come off to clean it properly.
before.solution: Remove the EGR valve and clean the diaphragm and pintle with carb cleaner, then snake out the EGR passages in the throttle body and intake plenum (this is required if cleaning only the valve does not clear the code). Replace the EGR gasket on reinstall. A new OEM valve is typically only needed if the diaphragm is torn or the electrical solenoid fails.
symptoms: Rough, surging, or hunting idle
Stalling at stops or when cold
Check engine light with P0400-series code
Failed emissions / smog test for high NOx or EGR flow
Hesitation or sputter during light acceleration

before.title: Front Suspension Knock from Worn Sway Bar End Links and Strut Mounts
before.description: RepairPal and MX-6 owner communities consistently identify a clunking or knocking sound from the front suspension over bumps and rough roads as one of the top complaints on 1993-1997 models. The most common cause is failed front sway bar end links, whose ball joints develop play and rattle. Worn upper strut mounts are a secondary cause, producing a similar knock plus steering imprecision. Both are inexpensive parts but are routinely missed during basic inspections.
before.solution: Inspect front sway bar end links for play in the ball joints; replace as a pair (inexpensive and quick). If knock persists, inspect upper strut mounts and bearings, and replace as needed - usually combined with new struts on cars of this age. Get a 4-wheel alignment after any front suspension work.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking over bumps from front of car
Rattle felt through steering wheel on rough pavement
Loose or imprecise on-center steering feel
Noise worsens at low speed over speed bumps

before.title: GF4A-EL Automatic Transmission Harsh Shifts and Failure
before.description: V6 MX-6s equipped with the GF4A-EL 4-speed automatic transmission suffer well-documented heat and pressure issues. Owners report harsh or slipping 1-2 and 2-3 shifts that progress over time to total loss of forward gears, frequently accompanied by burnt-smelling fluid. The transmission's solenoid valves wear quickly, clutch dust contaminates the valve body, and the electronics are heat-sensitive. Failure often occurs between 100,000-150,000 miles, especially on cars with no documented fluid service history. Mazda also issued no-start/no-shift TSBs related to the neutral safety/inhibitor switch on this transmission.
before.solution: Service ATF every 24,000 miles using only Mazda M-III or equivalent (Dexron III is acceptable per FSM). Add an auxiliary transmission cooler and external filter on cars used in hot climates or towing. A TransGo shift-correction kit improves shift quality and reduces clutch wear. Once burnt fluid is present, rebuild or replacement is typically required.
symptoms: Hard 1-2 or 2-3 upshifts
Slipping during shifts, high engine RPM with no acceleration
Burnt-smelling transmission fluid
Refuses to shift into gear from Park/Drive until cycled through neutral
Complete loss of drive after extended slipping

before.title: Timing Belt Failure Strands Car (Non-Interference but Stops Engine)
before.description: The KL-DE 2.5L V6 uses a rubber timing belt with a factory replacement interval of 60,000 miles. Original-owner neglect of this interval is extremely common on 2nd-gen MX-6s, leading to belt breakage. Fortunately the KL-DE is a non-interference design, so a snapped belt will not bend valves or damage pistons, but the car is immobilized until belt, tensioner, idlers, and (typically) the water pump are replaced. The water pump is driven by the timing belt, so it should always be replaced at the same time to avoid having to repeat the labor-intensive job. Two different water pump versions were used across early and late production, so the correct one must be ordered by year.
before.solution: Replace timing belt every 60,000 miles along with water pump, timing belt tensioner, and both idler pulleys. Use the correct water pump for the model year (early vs late production differs). Replace front crank seal and cam seals while accessible. Because the engine is non-interference, a snapped belt requires only belt-job parts, not valve work.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start after sudden stall
Loud slapping noise from front of engine immediately before failure
Coolant leak from front of engine (associated water pump failure)
Overheating or whining from front of engine

before.title: Distributor Failure on V6 Models
before.description: The MX-6 V6 (2.5L KL engine) distributor develops internal electronic failures, particularly the coil and crank angle sensor. The distributor is mounted at the rear of the engine between the heads, making it difficult to access and exposed to extreme heat. The failure causes intermittent no-start, stalling, and misfire conditions that are difficult to diagnose because they occur randomly.
before.solution: Replace the complete distributor assembly ($250-$450). The V6 distributor is located at the rear of the engine and requires removing the intake manifold for access (4-5 hours labor). Some owners carry a spare distributor in the trunk due to the intermittent nature of the failure. Test the crank angle sensor resistance before condemning the distributor — a simple resistance check can confirm the fault.
symptoms: Random no-start condition
Engine dies while driving
Intermittent misfires
Tachometer drops to zero while driving
No spark at any cylinder during no-start

before.title: Power Window Regulator Cable Snap
before.description: The MX-6's cable-type power window regulators are prone to cable snapping, causing the window to drop into the door. The cable frays at the pulley points and eventually breaks, leaving the window stuck in the down position. The frameless door design means a down window provides no weather protection. Both driver and passenger sides are affected, with the driver's side failing first due to higher usage.
before.solution: Replace the window regulator assembly ($80-$150 aftermarket). The repair requires removing the door panel, disconnecting the window from the regulator, and installing the new unit. Lubricate the window tracks and new regulator cables with silicone spray to reduce friction and extend life. The window motor can usually be reused if it still functions.
symptoms: Window drops into door suddenly
Window moves slowly or binds
Clicking noise from door when operating window
Window stops partway
Motor runs but window doesn't move
